bodies.notes: RENAME AND REORGANISATION (all effective 1-2 May 2025). Name: S.I. 180/2025 (in operation 2 May 2025) alters the name from Department of Children, Equality, Disability, Integration and Youth to Department of Children, Disability and Equality, and the Minister's title likewise: https://www.irishstatutebook.ie/pdf/2025/en.si.2025.0180.pdf . Functions OUT to Department of Justice: S.I. 159/2025, Integration and Reception (Transfer of Departmental Administration and Ministerial Functions) Order 2025, in operation 1 May 2025: international protection accommodation (IPAS) and procurement, State-owned centres for international protection, anti-racism policy and migrant integration and its funds, resettlement/temporary protection permissions, plus s.10(2)(l) of the IHREC Act 2014 insofar as it relates to promotion of integration of migrants, and Part 2 of the Civil Law (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 2022: https://www.irishstatutebook.ie/pdf/2025/en.si.2025.0159.pdf . Functions OUT to Department of Education: S.I. 181/2025, Youth (Transfer of Departmental Administration and Ministerial Functions) Order 2025, in operation 1 May 2025: functions under the Youth Work Act 2001; s.2(1)(d) and (2) of the Community, Rural and Gaeltacht Affairs (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 2007 in so far as they relate to the Young People's Facilities and Services Fund; s.10(1)(j) of the Education and Training Boards Act 2013; and funding, oversight and support of youth work organisations, youth organisations and ETB youth work functions, and youth policy: https://www.irishstatutebook.ie/pdf/2025/en.si.2025.0181.pdf . One small function back IN from Education: S.I. 185/2025 (1 May 2025) transfers the functions under s.18(4)(d) of the Youth Work Act 2001 to the children's department: https://www.irishstatutebook.ie/pdf/2025/en.si.2025.0185.pdf . Earlier (2020, not 2025): youth justice in the community went to the Department of Justice and Oberstown stayed (see iyjs). The three 2025 transfer orders themselves still use the old department name. Education side: Gaisce's 2025 annual report and Tusla's 2025 financial statements both name a 'Department of Education and Youth'; I did not read the order that renamed it. The Youth Participation page (last updated 10 March 2026) still shows the children's department running Comhairle na nÓg after the youth transfer. WHAT WAS READ: gov.ie blocks automated fetching (HTTP 403/405 and a bot-verification page, which I did not attempt to pass), so the department's own pages were read through Internet Archive snapshots of gov.ie (snapshot 5 Oct 2026; aegis page snapshot 16 Apr 2026); the three S.I.s from irishstatutebook.ie directly. The department's 'Functions and Services Provided to the Public' page is dated 2019 and still speaks of the Department of Children and Youth Affairs, so it was not used. Its 'Who Does What' page returned 403 even via the archive. Verdict part, not core: the stated mission sets children alongside disabled people and equality (see openQuestions).

bodies.notes: READ: tusla.ie About Us (remit), Commissioning page, Annual Report and Financial Statements 2025 PDF (searched for Section 56 text and appendices; not read in full). SECTION 56: the commissioning page and the 2025 financial statements both state that Tusla funds organisations under s.56 of the 2013 Act; the financial statements (note headed 'Community, Voluntary and Charitable Organisations') and the appendix titles call the funded organisations community, voluntary and charitable; the About and Commissioning pages do not use that wording. RECIPIENT LIST: YES, the 2025 Annual Report and Financial Statements publish a named recipient list - Appendix 3 (summary by grant type, with lines for ABC, CCA, CYPSC, Adoption, Disability, National Early Years, SCP, FRC, FSS Counselling), Appendix 4 (summary by grant type, service and region) and Appendix 5 'Community, Voluntary and Charitable Organisations by Providers', a numbered list of organisations with columns Section 56 All Other / SCP / FRC / Counselling / Total 2025 / Total 2024, in EUR '000. It is near the end of the PDF (printed pages c.205-208 onward): https://www.tusla.ie/uploads/content/Annual_Report_and_AFS_2025.pdf. Not extracted. Earlier years: https://www.tusla.ie/publications/annual-reports/ . Tusla is funded by two departments: the 2025 statements name funding received from the Department of Children, Disability and Equality (DCDE) and the Department of Education and Youth (DEY). Tusla is also the operational lead for CYPSC (see cypsc). The 193m and 38m figures are as printed in the summary panel; no conversion. The income and expenditure statement also has a 'Section 56-59 Arrangements' expenditure line, but the PDF text extraction garbled the column alignment, so it was not recorded.

bodies.name: Office of the Director of Authorised Intervention, Tuam
bodies.universeName: The Office of Director of Authorised Intervention
bodies.sponsor: Department of Children, Equality, Disability, Integration and Youth
bodies.currentSponsor: Department of Children, Disability and Equality
bodies.notes: READ: Institutional Burials Act 2022 (No. 18 of 2022), long title and s.10 functions of the Director (https://www.irishstatutebook.ie/eli/2022/act/18/enacted/en/print); S.I. 518/2022 (Director of Authorised Intervention, Tuam, Order 2022) and S.I. 87/2023 (Office stood established 20 March 2023, to continue in operation for 30 months from that date, i.e. to about September 2025; I could not establish whether it was extended or dissolved); and the department's gov.ie page on the Office via Internet Archive (https://web.archive.org/web/2026/https://www.gov.ie/en/department-of-children-disability-and-equality/publications/office-of-the-director-of-authorised-intervention-tuam). The functions are forensic excavation, recovery, analysis and final arrangements for human remains buried in a manifestly inappropriate manner on institutional land, and updates to relatives: none of that text is specific to children (the Act defines 'institution' as a residential facility for adults or children, or both). The Tuam site is a former Mother and Baby Institution, but no page read says the Office's function is about children as such, so none; this is arguable (see openQuestions). Other sources: https://www.irishstatutebook.ie/pdf/2022/en.si.2022.0518.pdf ; https://www.irishstatutebook.ie/pdf/2023/en.si.2023.0087.pdf . No annual report or accounts page found; no website of its own reached.

No amounts stated in what was read.

openQuestions: Department of Children, Disability and Equality is recorded 'part' because its own mission and Statement of Strategy put children alongside disabled people and equality (and the 2025 transfers took youth and integration out). Should it be core?

Office of the Director of Authorised Intervention, Tuam is recorded 'none': the Act and orders speak of human remains in institutions for 'adults or children, or both', not children; but the site is a former mother and baby institution and the sponsor is the children's department. Include as part/core on a judgement, or leave it out? Also unresolved: the Office was set up for 30 months from 20 March 2023; whether it was extended or closed in 2025 was not established.

Gaisce: core on a 14-25 programme (so partly adults), and its sponsor appears to have moved to the Department of Education and Youth (its own 2025 annual report), while the gov.ie aegis page (May 2025) still says the children's department is the primary funder. Which sponsor should the map show?

Irish Youth Justice Service: no page I read says in terms that it is a unit of the Department of Justice (it is on Justice's policy page, last updated April 2024, with a Justice contact address). Is that enough to place it there?
Tusla Section 56: the 2025 financial statements publish a named recipient list (Appendix 5; 473 s.56 organisations plus 124 SCP). A later stage must decide whether to extract it.

Source route: gov.ie blocks automated fetching, so the department, aegis, strategy, youth-participation, Tuam and Justice youth-justice pages were read via Internet Archive snapshots (URLs show the snapshot). Acceptable as the body's own documents?

Department of Education and Youth is the sponsor of Gaisce and a co-funder of Tusla; the order renaming the Education department was not read. The Department of Education batch should confirm its current name and remit.
